summary: The United States Army paused airstrikes against Iran, aligning with diplomatic talks between Oman and Iran to reopen the Hormuz Strait. Russian reconnaissance satellites have been monitoring Gulf states and U.S. installations, correlating with Iranian strikes. Israeli security incidents, including a drone crash near Minister Ben‑Gvir and IDF strikes killing Hamas operatives, underscore ongoing regional tensions.
key_points: On the night of July 27, the United States Army refrained from launching any strikes against Iran, as reported by Israeli security sources. This pause follows President Trump’s directive to suspend U.S. airstrikes, aligning with diplomatic efforts to keep the Hormuz Strait open. (Source: @inon_yttach/9668 and @asafroz/51911)

Omani officials arrived in Tehran on Friday to negotiate reopening of the Hormuz Strait. The talks progressed amid the U.S. decision to suspend strikes, aiming to secure safe passage for commercial shipping through the Strait. (Source: @asafroz/51911)

Since early July, Russian reconnaissance satellites have tracked activity over Gulf states and U.S. military installations, with imagery shared with Iran. The images correlate with Iranian strikes, suggesting coordination between Russian intelligence and Iranian operations. (Source: @asafroz/51904)

The U.S. Department of War reduced the death count attributed to the Iran war from 18 to 14 after four American soldiers died during Iranian strikes on U.S. bases in Jordan and Iraq. The reduction reflects post‑ceasefire hostilities. (Source: @Faytuks_Network/5741)
A Kuwaiti soldier reported Iranian missiles falling without U.S. air defense interception, indicating potential gaps in U.S. defensive coverage over Gulf airspace. (Source: @naya_foriraq/85605)

A drone crashed near the residence of Israeli internal security minister Itamar Ben‑Gvir in Khalil. The incident was reported by a local source, with details still under investigation. (Source: @kianmeli1/90073)

Israeli settlers set fire to a mosque in Qusra and sprayed Hebrew graffiti, prompting IDF troop deployment. A separate mosque in Kur, near Tulkarm, also burned with similar graffiti. IDF has not yet commented. (Source: @manniefabian/58858)

The IDF killed several Hamas operatives, including commander Muhannad Asaad Mahmoud Abu Ghazal in central Gaza, surveillance operative Raed Hani Mohammed in northern Gaza, and intelligence chief Nabhan Mohammed Nabhan al‑Amsi in Gaza City, during recent strikes. (Source: @manniefabian/58857)
